findings.title: BoardView `x` (stop) was a hardcoded flash advertising a capability the UI did not have
findings.detail: `x: () => flash('stop: no live agent process is owned by this TUI session')` fired unconditionally regardless of whether an agent was actually running — the UI advertised 'stop' in its footer (`x stop`) while the handler never checked real runtime state. The real capability existed all along: apps/desktop/src/main/agent/agent-manager.ts:740-742 `killTask(taskId): boolean` and :782-784 `isRunning(taskId): boolean` are plain public methods on the vendored AgentManager; they were simply never added to the TUI's service surface (AgentManagerLike in agent-start-service.ts only declared startTaskExecution/startRoadmapGeneration/startSpecCreation/stopRoadmap/isRoadmapRunning).
findings.fix_verified: Wired via a locally-scoped StoppableManager type (BoardView.tsx:30) rather than editing the shared agent-start-service.ts AgentManagerLike (out of scope for that fix). `x` now calls getManager(), checks isRunning(task.id) first (honest no-op reporting when no agent is live — never a silent no-op, always a flash naming the real state), and calls killTask(task.id) when one is. Verified live in a real PTY against a real fixture task with no live process: pressing `x` produced the toast 'test-spe: no live agent process for this task' — a genuine query result from the real AgentManager singleton, not a hardcoded string, with no runtime errors on getManager()/isRunning() resolution.

findings.title: applyAccountEnv() selected the active credential by providerAccounts[] insertion order, not by activation priority
findings.detail: applyAccountEnv() previously picked the exported account via `accounts.find((a) => a.provider === 'anthropic' && a.apiKey)` — array-INSERTION-order among providerAccounts[], hardcoded to anthropic, and completely ignoring globalPriorityOrder[]. ROADMAP.md's Phase 6 gate requires 'profile switch changes the active credential and the next agent run uses it'; P6.2's activateAccount() defines 'active' as the HEAD of globalPriorityOrder, not array position. With 2+ accounts this exported whichever sat earlier in providerAccounts[] regardless of which one the user just activated; with a non-anthropic active account it exported nothing and left stale ANTHROPIC_* vars from a previous session in place.
evidence: apps/tui/src/services/agent-start-service.ts:210-291 (applyAccountEnv, pre- and post-fix; the fix's own source comment carries this label as F-12, written before the F-12/F-14 renumbering below was settled — see cross_ref)
findings.fix_verified: Reuses buildDefaultQueueConfig() — the SAME function client/factory.ts's createSimpleClient()/createAgentClient() call internally, and the same contract account-service.ts's activateAccount() doc comment cites — instead of re-deriving the sort locally, so there is one source of truth for 'who is active'. Export is now provider-aware via BUILTIN_TO_SUPPORTED_PROVIDER + PROVIDER_ENV_VARS/PROVIDER_BASE_URL_ENV (auth/types.ts), not hardcoded to anthropic. Verified with a discriminating two-account fixture: providerAccounts fixed at [B, A] (insertion order B-then-A); with globalPriorityOrder head set to A, applyAccountEnv() exported identity A's credentials; with head set to B, it exported B's — confirming selection now tracks activation priority, not array position.

findings.title: `a` (add-Anthropic) binding cannot create a second Anthropic-compatible account
findings.detail: provisionAnthropicAccount() and its moonshot twin matched an existing account on `provider` ALONE (`a.provider === 'anthropic'`), so a second `a` press against a different Anthropic-compatible endpoint overwrote the first account's apiKey/baseUrl in place instead of appending a new one. An operator running two Anthropic-compatible routers (e.g. two different reverse-proxy endpoints) had no way to hold both accounts simultaneously — the second add silently clobbered the first.
evidence: apps/tui/src/services/account-service.ts:194 (pre-fix: `accounts.find((a) => a.provider === 'anthropic')`, no baseUrl in the match predicate)
findings.fix_verified: Match predicate is now `(provider, baseUrl)` — account-service.ts:194 reads `accounts.find((a) => a.provider === 'anthropic' && String(a.baseUrl ?? '') === baseUrl)` (moonshot twin at :114 does the same). Same endpoint still updates in place (keeps id + priority slot); a new endpoint now appends instead of overwriting. New `mintAccountId()` helper (account-service.ts:73-80) suffixes the minted id on a millisecond-clock collision so two appends in the same tick cannot clash. Verified live in a real PTY, isolated APERANT_USER_DATA home: two `a` presses against two different endpoints (http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1, http://127.0.0.1:20999/v1) produced TWO visible ACCOUNTS rows in Settings, both surviving on disk after restart.

findings.title: Unrecognized subagent type strings silently render under the wrong label in GraphView (`complexity_assessor` -> `spec_gatherer`)
findings.detail: observability.ts's new SUBAGENT_* task-event handler (added this session, P3.5.11 agentic-orchestration-optin) resolves a spawned subagent's display type via `(rawAgentType in AGENT_CONFIGS ? rawAgentType : 'spec_gatherer') as AgentType` before calling applyAgentType(). `complexity_assessor` is a valid SpawnSubagent input (SpawnSubagentInputSchema's agent_type enum, spawn-subagent.ts:24-38) but is NOT a key in AGENT_CONFIGS (confirmed by exhaustive grep of agent-configs.ts: zero occurrences of the string anywhere in that file) -- so any complexity_assessor spawn silently renders in GraphView/SwarmView under the label 'spec_gatherer', with no visible fallback indicator. This is distinct from, and layered on top of, a legitimate pre-existing design choice: subagent-executor.ts:44's resolveAgentType() deliberately maps complexity_assessor -> 'spec_gatherer' for TOOL-SET purposes only (its own comment: 'Uses spec_gatherer tools + complexity assessor prompt', since complexity_assessor needs a minimal read-only tool set and reuses spec_gatherer's). But the raw, unresolved agent_type string from the tool call (not the resolved AgentType) is what flows into the SUBAGENT_* task-event's agentType field, and observability.ts's independent DISPLAY-label fallback conflates the two -- a viewer cannot distinguish a real spec_gatherer spawn from a complexity_assessor spawn wearing that label. Confirmed materially relevant during the P3.5.11 live drive: two graph nodes labeled spec_gatherer appeared during a run where the swarm view was separately observed (ephemeral, not disk-captured) showing an agent id prefixed complexity_asses... with TYPE spec_gatherer -- i.e. the graph displayed a node type that never actually ran under that name.
evidence: apps/tui/src/services/observability.ts:369 (the display-label fallback: `(rawAgentType in AGENT_CONFIGS ? rawAgentType : 'spec_gatherer') as AgentType`)

apps/desktop/src/main/ai/orchestration/subagent-executor.ts:44 (pre-existing, legitimate tool-set-only mapping: `complexity_assessor: 'spec_gatherer', // Uses spec_gatherer tools + complexity assessor prompt`)
apps/desktop/src/main/ai/tools/builtin/spawn-subagent.ts:24-38 (SpawnSubagentInputSchema's agent_type enum, confirming complexity_assessor is a real, spawnable input)
apps/desktop/src/main/ai/config/agent-configs.ts (exhaustive grep: zero occurrences of the string complexity_assessor anywhere in the file's AGENT_CONFIGS keys)
evidence/phase-7/p3511-live/P3.5.11-LIVE.md ("Defect found: silent agent-type fallback mislabels graph nodes" section -- full trace and the live-drive observation that surfaced it)
findings.note: Not fixed this session, per explicit operator instruction: a display fallback that hides a type mismatch needs a deliberate design decision (surface the raw type verbatim? render a distinct 'unknown' label? emit a one-time warning trace event?) that is not this session's to make unilaterally. Recorded as a real defect in new code (unreachable before this session -- no code path constructed child AgentSnapshots at all prior to the P3.5.11 SUBAGENT_* wiring), not a regression in pre-existing behavior.
findings.fix_verified: observability.ts's AgentSnapshot now carries a new `rawType: string | null` field (added this session) alongside the existing `type: AgentType | 'unknown'`. The SUBAGENT_* handler (observability.ts:389) sets `child.snap.rawType = rawAgentType` unconditionally, BEFORE the existing AGENT_CONFIGS-key resolution/coercion runs — so the verbatim spawned string (e.g. `complexity_assessor`) is always preserved even when `type` gets coerced to `spec_gatherer` for grant-lookup purposes. AgentsView.tsx adds `displayType(a)` (prefers `rawType` over `type` when they disagree) and `isFallbackLabel(a)` (true iff a coercion occurred), and wires both into every render site that previously showed `a.type` verbatim: SwarmView's TYPE column (now shows the raw type plus a `⚠` marker in warn color), GraphView's root and child node labels (same treatment), and InspectView's `type` row (shows `<rawType> ⚠ unrecognized` in warn color, with an added `grants as` row disclosing which AGENT_CONFIGS key the grant lookup actually resolved to). A reader can therefore always see the real spawned type and, when it was unrecognized, both that fact and which config it borrowed grants from — no silent confident-wrong label remains possible. `AGENT_CONFIGS[type]`-keyed grant resolution (tools/mcpServers/autoClaudeTools) is untouched — `type` still resolves the same way it always did; only the DISPLAY layer changed. `subagent-executor.ts:44`'s `complexity_assessor -> spec_gatherer` tool-set mapping is unchanged, per operator instruction (it is a legitimate pre-existing design decision, not the defect). `npm run typecheck` (root, resolving to @aperant/tui via tsconfig paths) is clean, exit 0, confirmed this session after the edit.
findings.residual: The `⚠` fallback marker and `grants as` row are new UI surface, not yet exercised against a live SUBAGENT_* event carrying an actually-unrecognized rawAgentType in a real running process (the live drive in evidence/phase-7/subagent-proof/ re-attempts that capture; if a complexity_assessor spawn is observed there, its label should now read the raw type with the warning marker instead of a bare 'spec_gatherer').

findings.title: SwarmView's WAITING ON column always reads '— executing' for subagent-spawned rows, including done/error terminal states
findings.detail: AgentsView.tsx's SwarmView renders two independent per-row status signals: the leading glyph (`STATE_GLYPH[a.state]`, AgentsView.tsx:207 -- correctly bound to `snap.state`, confirmed to show `✓`/`✗` for done/error) and a separate WAITING ON column (`waitText(a.waiting)`, AgentsView.tsx:212). `waitText()` (AgentsView.tsx:85-95) has cases only for the six `WaitState.kind` variants (tool/mcp/concurrency/context/ratelimit/auth) and a single fallback for `null`: the literal string `'— executing'` -- it has no representation of `done` or `error` terminal states at all, because `WaitState` (observability.ts:39-47) was designed purely to describe *why a running agent is blocked*, not to carry terminal status. observability.ts's SUBAGENT_SPAWNING/SUBAGENT_COMPLETED/SUBAGENT_FAILED handler (onTaskEvent, lines 379-397) correctly sets `child.snap.state` (spawning->running, completed->done, failed->error) but never touches `child.snap.waiting` -- and no other code path does either: `recomputeWait()` (the sole writer of `.waiting`, line 492) is called only from `onStreamEvent()` (tool-call/tool-result/step-finish/usage-update handlers) and `pollSentinels()`; `onTaskEvent()` never calls it. A subagent's own internal tool-call/step-finish stream events are never relayed to the parent process's observability tap at all -- confirmed by exhaustive grep of worker.ts and subagent-executor.ts: the only `postMessage` carrying a subagent's `subagentId` is the single `task-event` SUBAGENT_* payload (worker.ts:1052-1062); no `stream-event` ever keys off a child `subagentId`. So a SUBAGENT_*-driven child's `snap.waiting` is set once to `null` at `ensureAgent()`'s init (observability.ts:283) and is never written again for the rest of that child's lifetime -- `waitText(null)` therefore always renders '— executing' for every subagent-spawned row, spawning through done or failed, with no code path capable of changing it. Live-observed: evidence/phase-7/subagent-proof-v2/captures/step-03-final-swarm-six-completed.png shows a root row (glyph ✓, real `snap.waiting`-driven WAITING ON text via the normal onStreamEvent path since the root DOES receive stream-events) alongside six subagent rows whose glyphs read ✓✗✓✓✓✓✓ (correctly matching their real `SUBAGENT_COMPLETED`/`SUBAGENT_FAILED` terminal states, cross-checked against evidence/phase-7/subagent-proof-v2/work-product/task_logs.json's six disk-backed 'completed successfully' entries) but every one of whose WAITING ON columns reads the identical, unconditional '— executing', including the two rows (glyph ✓) that had already reached SUBAGENT_COMPLETED at capture time and the one row (glyph ✗) that had already reached SUBAGENT_FAILED. This is a genuine display gap, not a capture-timing artifact: no timing exists under which this column would ever read anything else for a subagent row, because no code path ever writes to it after child creation.
evidence: apps/tui/src/services/observability.ts:39-47 (`WaitState` union: six blocking-reason kinds only, no terminal-state variant)
apps/tui/src/services/observability.ts:283 (`ensureAgent()` default snapshot: `waiting: null`, set once at creation)

apps/desktop/src/main/ai/agent/worker.ts:1052-1062 (the only `postMessage` carrying a `subagentId` is the `task-event` SUBAGENT_* payload; no `stream-event` for any child `subagentId` exists in worker.ts or subagent-executor.ts, confirmed by grep)

evidence/phase-7/subagent-proof-v2/captures/step-03-final-swarm-six-completed.png (live capture: six subagent rows, glyphs correctly showing ✓✗✓✓✓✓✓ for real done/error states, WAITING ON column identically '— executing' on every one)

evidence/phase-7/subagent-proof-v2/work-product/task_logs.json (disk-backed cross-check: six real SUBAGENT_COMPLETED / one SUBAGENT_FAILED entries matching the glyphs, contradicting the WAITING ON text)
findings.note: Not fixed this session, per explicit operator instruction: recording the finding and leaving the fix scope decision to the operator, since this session has already made two display-layer changes (F-19's rawType/displayType wiring) and a third unilateral change was declined.
